retrieval_query: Adam optimizer bias correction and update rule

turns.user_message: Explain Adam optimizer in 6 technical bullets. Every bullet must cite the supporting chunk.

output.text:
* Initialization bias can be counteracted easily to produce bias-corrected estimates $m$ and $v$ [1412.6980v9.pdf::chunk0016].
* Assuming $\epsilon = 0$, the effective step taken in parameter space at timestep $t$ is defined as $\Delta_t = \alpha \hat{m}_t / \sqrt{\hat{v}_t}$ [1412.6980v9.pdf::chunk0016].
* Removing bias-correction terms causes values of $\beta$ close to 1 to produce infinitely large bias and infinitely large parameter updates [1412.6980v9.pdf::chunk0040].
* Without a bias-correction term, setting $\beta$ close to 1 leads to training instabilities, particularly during the initial epochs of training [1412.6980v9.pdf::chunk0060].
* The absence of a bias-correction term in RMSProp causes very large stepsizes and often leads to divergence when $\beta$ is close to 1 for sparse gradients [1412.6980v9.pdf::chunk0038].
* Optimal empirical results are achieved using small values of $(1 - \beta)$ combined with bias correction, especially as gradients grow sparser toward the end of optimization [1412.6980v9.pdf::chunk0060].
